children: ADES Holding Company said it has secured multi-year contracts for two standard jack-up rigs with Indian government-backed Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC).

The contract is a three-year firm contract for each rig, with total contract value, including mobilisation fees, of nearly 439.6 million Saudi riyals ($117.2 million), the company said in a statement to the Saudi stock exchange.

The jack-up rigs - Key Singapore and Admarine 10 - are expected to commence operations by the end of the first quarter of 2027, following the completion of the rigs’ existing campaigns by the end of the fourth quarter of 2026.
The awards further strengthen ADES’ position in India and reflect the continued demand for offshore jackup capacity.
Operations are expected to commence by the end of the first quarter of 2027, following the completion of the rigs’ existing campaigns by the end of the fourth quarter of 2026.

India has allocated INR 432 billion ($4.6 billion) for accelerated offshore exploration, including drilling 60 deepwater exploration wells. The government expects the programme to add more than 600 million tonnes of oil equivalent to India’s hydrocarbon reserves and substantially increase domestic oil and gas production.

title: Saudi ADES wins offshore rig contract from India’s ONGC
